approach.method_basis: The Parent repeatedly breeds a fresh field of molecular graphs from its scored population and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process using only accepted feedback from the current objective. It draws 10,000 correlated latent score functions, counts each field member's wins, and purchases the molecules with the most wins, breaking ties by predicted mean and original field order. After three non-improving batches, an inherited screen limits both winner counting and purchases to the forty highest predicted means. Accepted scores update the archive and score-greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove that stalled top-forty screen from winner counting and purchase eligibility, while retaining the same posterior, all 10,000 correlated draws, and the stall state as a passive diagnostic. This opens access to candidates the screen excludes and tests whether their actual feedback produces useful progress. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in the frozen brief; the concurrent tickets separately test the probability objective and allocation correlation. Earlier screen-release work used sequential Thompson choices and a delayed release, so it does not answer this all-or-none screen question under winner-probability selection.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-0eae06e8d311 restricts 63 of 435 announcements to forty candidates although its fresh field contains 160. The source-checked fifteen Search audits find 184 full-field winners outside that mask among the 630 logged first rows on those restricted announcements. This establishes naturally exposed domain exclusion, not the full-10,000-row alternative batch or any unpurchased score. qPO itself executed exactly with no fallback: its complete macro is 0.5580387031939377 versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de at 0.607030316211131, with all three seed macro differences negative. The additive Analyze/Molecular v2 corrections give full incumbent-gain mass 5.243198882274432 versus 5.978073077532332 on 4350 purchases despite 300 versus 253 incumbent updates; late mass is 1.335237861278773 versus 1.0224077547621127 on 2175 purchases. Thus useful full-run conversion limits this Parent, and its inherited mean screen is an exposed but unpriced consumer. n-61b9b3bfb40d's mask history and n-5911390da209's non-positive delayed-release result concern a different active acquisition law; neither establishes this screen's contribution on qPO. Evidence is audited in policy/scratch/r0059-01-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and its fifteen task/seed audits with the underlying published logs and trajectories.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review search-policy-r59-conditional-transfer-and-consumer-interactions exactly as provenance and applicability context. Carry only its two directly relevant primary sources; do not claim a new literature adoption. The source setting is finite-library pre-filtering, the retained campaign setting is task-local fresh-field de novo qPO, and the deliberate control deviation is all-or-none removal of only the inherited stalled top-forty domain consumer. Direct exposure supports this testable question but supplies no score for excluded molecules and no guarantee of benefit.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: This is the ticket-frozen removal of an existing domain consumer, motivated by direct natural-exposure receipts on n-0eae06e8d311 and the unresolved conditional contribution of m-61b9b3bfb40d. No new source method is introduced. The paper evaluates finite-library screening and filtered domains; this campaign already generates fresh molecular fields under a latent GP. Deliberately omitting the inherited stall screen isolates that existing implementation's applicability condition while retaining its winner objective, covariance, all draws and paid-feedback protocol. The source paper's filtering comparison cannot supply the result of this control.

hypothesis: Remove only the consumption of the stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility mask by fixed-field qPO. For every successful allocation, let E be every admitted current-pool index and recompute all 10000 row winners over E using the original stable first-index maximum. Count one winner per row, then select the announced batch by (-winner_count,-original_mean,pool_index). Keep the original K=3 stall state and its mean-ranked top-forty mask E_parent as passive diagnostics. The hypothesized path is full-domain winner redistribution -> actual outside-E_parent purchases on naturally stalled states -> accepted feedback that can yield direct or later productive progress. The intervention makes no claim that wider access or higher model probability must improve real scores.

finding_summary.headline: Full-domain access works, but removing the stall screen reduces useful progress and scores
finding_summary.insights: The stall screen has a positive conditional endpoint contribution on this qPO composition at the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its removal was neither dormant nor technically unsuccessful, and missing outside feedback no longer explains the result. Yet the effect cannot be attributed solely to outside purchases: recounting over the full field also changes rankings within the old screen, and one session changed its paid decisions without buying an outside molecule. Later feedback and breeding histories then diverge. The selected outside group exposes a useful limitation: its average prediction overstatement was 0.0820 versus 0.0187 for stalled inside-screen purchases, its prediction MSE was 0.0201 versus 0.0060, and 33 of its 75 purchases were fragments below twelve heavy atoms, none with direct gain. Only 25 survived their batch and eight bred later. Broad access therefore reached structures that the current surrogate and graph proposals converted poorly into useful outcomes. A better ranking or calibration model, or graph operators that preserve coherent molecular frameworks, could address that limitation; these observations do not establish which would work, justify a size gate, or imply missing biological features. Overall typed/generic scaffold counts also fell from 1,982/1,203 to 1,938/1,170 while both size tails grew, so broader eligibility did not create broader realized scaffold coverage. The Molecular assessment further shows unresolved heteroatom-halogen chemistry and unspecified stereochemistry, descriptive limitations shared with the generator rather than proven causes of this loss. Three outside origins had 206 paid descendant memberships and 0.05114 gain summed over origins, but those chains overlap and end at the fixed horizon; they cannot be treated as causal recovery or added to direct gain. This result settles this consumer contrast under the retained posterior and sampling law. It leaves alternative proposal/ranking methods and other qPO compositions open, and supplies no reliable-generalization claim or decision to end the approach.
finding_summary.results: All 435 allocations preserved the intended 10,000-draw law, and independent replay reproduced their original posteriors, random states, active counts and passive restricted counts exactly. The 57 naturally stalled announcements changed 142,158 of 570,000 row winners and produced 75 outside-screen purchases across 12 of 15 sessions. The 378 unrestricted announcements matched the inherited law exactly. Outside-screen purchases supplied one direct incumbent improvement worth 0.001547, and three outside origins had later paid descendants. This was real exposure, but it did not improve overall progress: full-run incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.24320 to 5.11213 and late gain from 1.33524 to 1.26997. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.558039 to 0.549301, a paired loss of 0.008738, with all three seed macros negative. The separate formal Anchor deficit was 0.057729. Zaleplon and sitagliptin also breached the Parent task-regression margins. The allocation/access mechanism is confirmed; the registered useful-progress and score-benefit prediction is refuted.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring-rich offspring retain reactive heteroatom motifs, unspecified stereochemistry and both molecular-size tails.
molecular.overall_character: Child n-0e978ade2613 and published code Parent n-0eae06e8d311 have complete Search trajectories and complete paired evaluation on seeds [0, 1, 2]; no supplied task is absent. All chemistry describes accepted evaluated output, not the unseen proposal field. Each side contains 4350 optimizer observations; the late window has 2175 at paid ordinals 146 through 290. The Child has median 31.0 heavy atoms, range 1 to 115; Parent median 31.0, range 1 to 120. Full below-twelve/above-fifty counts are 170/202 versus 143/194; late counts are 72/84 versus 58/73. Ring and aromatic content are substantial; digest ring-closure/aromatic rates are text indicators, not RDKit ring counts. Full unique nonempty typed/generic Murcko counts are 1938/1170 versus 1982/1203; late 857/474 versus 879/516. Fragment-excluded radius-two sparse-count Morgan mean within-batch/nearest-preceding-archive similarity is 0.5176721170581149/0.7627759142770351 versus 0.5244894529674543/0.7645196300413494. Both query and comparison require at least twelve heavy atoms; archive excludes the current batch. Structural coverage does not establish useful access or component attribution. Broad graph diversity coexists with locally related terminal families and questionable N-halogen, O-halogen, imine, thione and strained-ring chemistry. RDKit finds 902 N-halogen-bearing Child molecules versus 653 Parent; these are substructure flags, not reactivity assays. 2807 Child molecules have potential unassigned tetrahedral centres, while 0 have specified centres. Neutral SMILES do not demonstrate absent basicity. Full/late incumbent-gain sums are 5.1121308934935605/1.2699679919880185 versus 5.243198882274431/1.3352378612787732; these sum observed sequential increments and make no intervention claim. Actual outside-passive-screen paid subsets contain 75 full and 51 late molecules, with gain 0.001547282718770221/0. Their task/seed sizes, both tails, scaffold coverage and fragment-excluded similarities, including empty groups, are recorded in policy/scratch/r0059-01-improve-L01-molecular/outside-index.json and its listed group files. No outcome is assigned to unpurchased alternatives. Survival and descendant attribution are absent from this molecular audit and remain Analyze work. All thirty exact trajectories were read; no missing trajectory or Parent pairing is inferred. Do not convert this descriptive association into a universal size gate or a claim that larger scaffold counts ensure useful exploration.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
